concepts.name: Business activity, needs and wants, and the factors of production
concepts.description: Why people produce: needs and wants, goods (consumer and producer goods) and services, scarcity, choice and opportunity cost; the production function (inputs, processes, outputs); the four factors of production (land, labour, capital, enterprise) and their rewards (rent, wages, interest, profit). [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Stages and sectors of production
concepts.description: Primary (extractive), secondary (manufacturing and construction) and tertiary (commercial and direct services) production; the chain of production from raw material to consumer; interdependence of the sectors; how commerce (trade and the aids to trade) relates to production; changes in the importance of the sectors as an economy develops. Not private and public sector (see bus.organisation.purpose-sectors). [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Ownership of the means of production
concepts.description: Why it matters who owns land, minerals and capital; land as heritage; land reform; indigenisation and economic empowerment; the role of government in widening local ownership of the economy. Neutral, factual treatment of policy. [COM]

concepts.name: Direct and indirect production, division of labour and mass production
concepts.description: Direct production (producing for one's own use) and indirect production (producing for exchange); division of labour and specialisation (by person, process, region and country), their advantages and disadvantages; mass production. [COM]

concepts.name: Adding value: value addition and beneficiation
concepts.description: Added value as the difference between the selling price and the cost of bought-in materials and how a business can increase it (branding, quality, processing, convenience, service); value addition and beneficiation of Zimbabwe's minerals and agricultural produce at each stage of production; benefits to the producer, the community and the country. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Methods of production: job, batch and flow
concepts.description: Job, batch and flow production, their features, advantages and disadvantages, and recommending a method for a given business. [CAM]

concepts.name: Productivity, efficiency and lean production
concepts.description: Calculating labour productivity (output per employee per period); why efficiency matters and how to raise it (automation, technology, better labour skills); lean production through just-in-time inventory control and Kaizen, with advantages and disadvantages. [CAM]

concepts.name: Purchasing and inventory management
concepts.description: The purchasing function and its importance; the five rights of purchasing (right quality, quantity, price, time, source/supplier); the purchasing cycle and e-purchasing; types of inventory (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods); why businesses hold inventory, the costs and benefits of holding it and the factors that affect how much is held. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Technology and ICT in production and operations
concepts.description: Automation and mechanisation, computer-aided design and manufacture (CAD/CAM), 3D printing, bar codes, radio frequency identification (RFID), electronic stock control, online billing and contactless payments in services; advantages and disadvantages of new technology for businesses and employees; recommending ICT tools for a given enterprise. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Sustainable production and use of resources
concepts.description: How businesses can produce sustainably: renewable energy, using fewer resources and less waste, reusing, recycling, environmentally friendly products and packaging; sustainable use of land, water, forests and wildlife; advantages and disadvantages for a business of becoming more sustainable. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Business costs
concepts.description: Fixed, variable, total and average costs, direct and indirect costs; calculating total variable cost, total cost and average cost; using cost data to make simple decisions (what to produce, whether to continue, what price to set, which supplier). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Economies and diseconomies of scale
concepts.description: Purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial and technical economies of scale; diseconomies of scale (poor communication, low commitment of employees, weak coordination, lack of control). [CAM]

concepts.name: Break-even analysis: calculations
concepts.description: The concept of break-even; contribution per unit (selling price minus variable cost per unit); calculating break-even output and break-even revenue; calculating and interpreting the margin of safety; the effect on break-even of changes in price, fixed costs and variable cost per unit. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Break-even charts and the uses and limits of break-even
concepts.description: Constructing, completing and amending a simple break-even chart (fixed cost, total cost and revenue lines); reading the break-even point, the profit and loss regions and the margin of safety from a chart; using break-even to make decisions; limitations of break-even analysis. Charts are described in words or tables. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Quality of goods and services
concepts.description: What quality means and why it matters; quality control and quality assurance and their advantages and disadvantages; total quality management (TQM), quality circles; recommending quality control or assurance for a business. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Location and relocation of a business
concepts.description: Factors influencing the location of manufacturing and service businesses (raw materials, markets, transport, labour, power and water, government policy, competitors), deciding which country to operate in, and why businesses relocate (depletion of raw materials, dying markets, natural disasters, government policy); recommending a location. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Introduction to trade
concepts.description: Why people trade; barter and its problems compared with trade using money; the branches of trade (home trade: retail and wholesale; foreign trade: imports, exports, entrepot) and the aids to trade (transport, communication, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising). [COM]

concepts.name: Wholesale trade, marketing boards and commodity markets
concepts.description: Services of wholesalers to manufacturers, retailers and consumers; types of wholesaler (general, specialist, cash and carry, co-operative wholesale societies); why and how wholesalers are bypassed; marketing boards (for example the Grain Marketing Board) and their functions; commodity markets and their functions. [COM]

concepts.name: Retail trade: functions and types of retailer
concepts.description: Functions of retailers to producers, wholesalers and consumers; small-scale retailers (tuck shops, kiosks, market stalls, hawkers and vendors, mobile shops) and large-scale retailers (supermarkets, hypermarkets, chain stores, department stores), their characteristics and organisation; factors to consider when opening a retail outlet; why small-scale retailers survive. [COM]

concepts.name: E-commerce and trends in retailing
concepts.description: Trends in retailing (self-service, electronic point of sale, bar coding, vending machines, loyalty schemes) and e-commerce: online shopping, mobile phone and internet banking, online ticketing; advantages and disadvantages of e-commerce for businesses and for customers. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Hire purchase, credit sales and other forms of credit
concepts.description: Hire purchase and deferred payment (credit sale) agreements, credit cards and informal credit (for example credit from a local shop); main features, advantages and disadvantages, comparing hire purchase with deferred payment, and how hire purchase is financed. [COM]

concepts.name: Documents used in home trade, and trade and cash discounts
concepts.description: Letter of enquiry, quotation, price list and catalogue, order, pro forma invoice, invoice, delivery and advice notes, debit and credit notes, statement of account and receipt: contents, purpose and sequence; trade discount and cash discount, their purposes and calculations (trade discount first, then cash discount). [COM]

concepts.name: Foreign trade: reasons, difficulties and intermediaries
concepts.description: Why countries trade (interdependence, specialisation, obtaining what cannot be produced at home); difficulties faced by importers and exporters (distance, currency, language, regulations, payment risk); entrepot trade; intermediaries in foreign trade (brokers, merchants, factors and agents) and how they differ. [COM]

concepts.name: Documents and customs in foreign trade
concepts.description: Indent, consular invoice, letter of credit, bill of exchange, customs specification (declaration), certificate of origin, airway bill and bill of lading: purpose and key information; functions of customs authorities (the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority, ZIMRA): collecting duties, preventing smuggling, controlling bonded warehouses, collecting trade statistics. [COM]

concepts.name: Free trade, protectionism, tariffs and quotas
concepts.description: Free trade versus protection; methods of restricting trade (tariffs, quotas, embargoes, exchange control); reasons for protection; effects of import tariffs and quotas on businesses, consumers and the economy. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Trading blocs and economic integration
concepts.description: Economic integration and trading blocs such as SADC, COMESA, ECOWAS, the AU and the EU: aims, features, member states (examples), advantages and disadvantages, and effects on Zimbabwe's economy and businesses. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Balance of trade and balance of payments
concepts.description: Visible and invisible trade; calculating the balance of trade, the invisible balance and the balance of payments on current account; causes of a deficit and ways of correcting it. [COM]

concepts.name: Warehousing: functions and importance
concepts.description: What warehousing is, its functions (storage, protection, packing, breaking bulk, stabilising prices, seasonal supply) and importance to trade; indigenous storage systems (for example granaries: dura, isiphala, tsapi). [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Types of warehouse and warehouse location
concepts.description: Private warehouses (manufacturers', wholesalers', retailers'), public warehouses and bonded warehouses and their functions; factors to consider when locating a warehouse. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Importance of transport and modes of transport
concepts.description: Why transport matters to commerce; the development of transport; road, rail, air, water and pipeline transport, their characteristics, advantages and disadvantages and suitable goods for each. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Choosing a mode of transport, transport documents and ports
concepts.description: Factors influencing the choice of transport (cost, speed, distance, nature and value of goods, safety, reliability, urgency, accessibility); transport documents (consignment note, delivery note, bill of lading, airway bill); the role of port authorities and how a landlocked country uses sea ports and inland (dry) ports. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Trends in transport
concepts.description: Containerisation, toll gates, vehicle tracking systems, e-ticketing, satellite positioning (GPS), the growth of air cargo and the impact of ICT on transport, with advantages and disadvantages. [COM]

concepts.name: Consumer rights, responsibilities and the need for protection
concepts.description: Why consumers need protection and how they can be exploited (short measures, false descriptions, unsafe or expired goods, overpricing); consumer rights and responsible consumer behaviour. [COM]

concepts.name: Consumer protection organisations
concepts.description: Roles of consumer protection bodies such as the Consumer Council of Zimbabwe (CCZ) and the Standards Association of Zimbabwe (SAZ), and how consumers use them. [COM]

concepts.name: Legal controls and government action to protect consumers
concepts.description: Methods of protecting consumers: legislation against misleading promotion and faulty or unsafe goods, weights and measures, labelling, price controls, the role of government, and self-protection by consumers; effects of legal controls on businesses and their marketing. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Purpose of business organisations; private and public sectors
concepts.description: Why business organisations exist (meeting needs, employment creation, income, infrastructure and development); the private sector and the public sector, classifying business units into each; the formal and informal sectors. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Sole traders and partnerships
concepts.description: Features, formation, ownership and control of sole proprietorships and partnerships; the partnership deed; unlimited liability; advantages and disadvantages; setting up a sole proprietorship or partnership; recommending a form for given owners. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Private and public limited companies
concepts.description: Features, ownership (shareholders) and control (directors) of private and public limited companies; differences between them; advantages and disadvantages; recommending a type of business organisation for a given situation. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Forming a company: legal personality, limited liability and documents
concepts.description: Separate legal personality and limited liability and why they matter; risks of forming a new enterprise; documents for forming a company (memorandum of association, articles of association, certificate of incorporation, trading certificate, prospectus) and their contents. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Franchises, joint ventures and social enterprises
concepts.description: How franchises work, advantages and disadvantages for franchisor and franchisee; joint ventures and their advantages and disadvantages; social enterprises; comparing forms of business enterprise. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Public sector organisations
concepts.description: Public corporations (parastatals), local authorities, government departments and public marketing boards: features, functions, ownership and control, merits and demerits. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Commercialisation, privatisation and nationalisation
concepts.description: Meaning of commercialisation, privatisation and nationalisation and the arguments for and against each. [COM]

concepts.name: Multinational companies
concepts.description: Features of multinational companies (MNCs); why a business becomes an MNC; advantages and disadvantages for the host country (jobs, exports, investment, choice; competition, environmental damage, exploitation of resources, repatriation of profits) and for the home country. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Small to medium enterprises
concepts.description: Features of small to medium enterprises (SMEs), including informal-sector and home-industry businesses; their importance to Zimbabwe's economy; the challenges they face; government programmes and assistance for SMEs (for example grants, loans, workspace at home-industry sites). [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Traders' associations and business membership organisations
concepts.description: Traders' associations (for example associations of vendors or booksellers) and business membership organisations such as the Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce (ZNCC), the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) and ZimTrade: functions and importance. [COM]

concepts.name: Enterprise and entrepreneurs
concepts.description: Meaning of enterprise, enterprising and entrepreneur (enterpriser); skills and personal qualities of successful entrepreneurs (leadership, innovation, creativity, risk-taking, determination); benefits and drawbacks of being an entrepreneur; importance of enterprise to the economy. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The role of the enterpriser and drivers towards enterprise
concepts.description: What an enterpriser does (scanning the environment, identifying opportunities, mobilising and allocating resources, setting up and managing the business) and what drives people to start enterprises (government policy, demographic and economic change, self-actualisation, community role models). [BES]

concepts.name: Business opportunities and risks
concepts.description: How business opportunities arise (unmet demand, new technology, research and development, changes in tastes, population and real income, globalisation, government policy) and the risks enterprisers face; judging the likelihood and impact of a risk. [BES]

concepts.name: Support for new businesses
concepts.description: Why new enterprises need support and why governments support start-ups; how they are supported (grants, low-cost loans, advice, training schemes, help from family and friends, fundraising). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The business plan
concepts.description: Purpose and importance of a business plan; its main sections (executive summary, business background, products, market research and analysis, marketing, operations, management and people, financial plan); drafting a simple business plan. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The business planning process and implementing a plan
concepts.description: Steps in business planning: purpose (destiny, cause and calling), setting objectives, generating, evaluating and selecting options, implementation, review and control; implementing and managing a business plan on a project. [BES]

concepts.name: Business objectives
concepts.description: Objectives such as survival, growth, profit, sales revenue, market share, corporate social responsibility and ethical aims; why objectives are important and how they change. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Stakeholders
concepts.description: Internal stakeholders (owners, managers, employees) and external stakeholders (customers, suppliers, lenders, government, local community, competitors); their roles and objectives; how stakeholder objectives conflict. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Measuring business size; small and large businesses
concepts.description: Methods of measuring business size (number of employees, value or volume of output or sales, capital employed; not profit) and their problems; advantages and disadvantages of being small or large; why some businesses remain small. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Business growth
concepts.description: Why owners want growth; factors influencing growth; internal growth (new products, new markets) and external growth (mergers, takeovers; horizontal and vertical integration); advantages and disadvantages of each method; problems and effects of growth. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Why businesses succeed or fail
concepts.description: Causes of business failure (poor management, poor record keeping, lack of finance, unsuitable product, low demand, economic change, competition) and of success, and solutions to the causes of failure. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Business ethics and social responsibility
concepts.description: Ethical issues in business (fair wages, fair prices to suppliers, child labour, honest advertising, bribery, environmentally responsible suppliers); the role and importance of ethics to business and society; corporate social responsibility; advantages and disadvantages of being ethical. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Intellectual property
concepts.description: Types of intellectual property (patents, trademarks, copyright, industrial designs, geographical indications); why they are protected; infringements such as piracy and plagiarism and their remedies; functions of the Zimbabwe patents office, ARIPO and WIPO. [COM]

concepts.name: The business environment: internal and external factors
concepts.description: Internal environment (owners, employees, resources, management, culture) and external environment (customers, suppliers, competitors; political, economic, social, technological, legal and ecological factors); business constraints; SWOT analysis; how each factor affects a business. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Resources and capabilities of an enterprise
concepts.description: Tangible resources (land, water, forests, buildings, capital) and intangible resources (knowledge, skills, expertise, reputation); capabilities; why resources and capabilities are analysed; ways of acquiring and owning resources. [BES]

concepts.name: The business cycle and economic change
concepts.description: Stages of the business cycle (growth, boom, recession, slump) and how each affects businesses; effects of changes in employment, inflation and economic growth on a business. [CAM]

concepts.name: Effects of government economic policy
concepts.description: Effects of changes in taxes (on profits and on people's income), government spending and interest rates on businesses, and how businesses may respond. [CAM]

concepts.name: Globalisation
concepts.description: Reasons for globalisation (transport links, technology and communication, free trade agreements, newly industrialised countries) and the opportunities and threats it brings to businesses. [CAM]

concepts.name: Exchange rates
concepts.description: Appreciation and depreciation of an exchange rate and how changes affect importers and exporters (prices, costs, competitiveness); converting amounts between currencies at a given rate (ZIMSEC Commerce only: Cambridge does not assess exchange-rate calculations). [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: External costs and benefits
concepts.description: External (social) costs and benefits of business decisions, such as a new factory or mine, for the community and the environment. [CAM]

concepts.name: Business and the environment
concepts.description: How business activity can damage the environment (pollution, depletion of resources); why and how businesses respond to environmental issues; effects of legal controls on what, how and where businesses produce or sell, and on costs. [CAM]

concepts.name: Pressure groups
concepts.description: What pressure groups are and how they influence business decisions (publicity, boycotts, lobbying), and how businesses respond. [CAM]

concepts.name: The functions of management and delegation
concepts.description: Planning, organising, commanding (directing, leading), coordinating and controlling; the importance of each; advantages and disadvantages of delegation. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Organisational structure
concepts.description: Functional areas (operations, marketing, finance, human resources); hierarchy, tall and flat structures, chain of command and span of control; reading simple organisation charts; flexible working (home working, flexible hours); part-time and full-time employees. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Leadership
concepts.description: Qualities of a good leader; autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership styles, their advantages and disadvantages, and recommending a style for a situation. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Why people work and motivation theories
concepts.description: Why people work; benefits of a well-motivated workforce (productivity, lower absenteeism and labour turnover, acceptance of change); the theories of Maslow, Taylor and Herzberg (and McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y for ZIMSEC) and how they apply to businesses. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Financial and non-financial methods of motivation
concepts.description: Financial methods (time rate, piece rate, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing, fringe benefits) and non-financial methods (job enrichment, job rotation, training, promotion, praise, employee of the month); recommending a method for a situation. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Recruitment and selection
concepts.description: The recruitment process (job description, person specification, job advertisement, employment agencies, online recruitment); internal and external recruitment; selection methods (CV, application form, references, tests, interviews); recommending whom to employ. [CAM]

concepts.name: Employment contracts and legal controls over employment
concepts.description: Main contents of an employment contract and its benefits to employer and employee; legal controls over unfair dismissal, discrimination, health and safety and minimum wages, and their effects on employers and employees. [CAM]

concepts.name: Training
concepts.description: Importance of training to a business and to employees; induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training and their advantages and disadvantages. [CAM]

concepts.name: Downsizing and redundancy
concepts.description: Downsizing and why a business may reduce its workforce (automation, lower demand, cutting costs); redundancy compared with dismissal; deciding which employees to make redundant. [CAM]

concepts.name: Trade unions
concepts.description: What a trade union is and the benefits to employees of membership. [CAM]

concepts.name: Communication in business: importance and methods
concepts.description: Meaning and importance of communication; internal and external communication; oral, written, visual and electronic methods (meetings, letters, memos, notices, phone calls, text messages, email, social media); advantages and disadvantages; factors in choosing a method (cost, urgency, reliability, need for a record); recommending a method. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Effective communication and communication barriers
concepts.description: What makes communication effective (enhancers); examples and causes of barriers (jargon, language, noise, poor channels, attitudes, too long a chain of command); problems they cause and how to reduce or remove them. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Telecommunication services and service providers
concepts.description: Telecommunication devices and services (fixed telephone, mobile phone, internet, data services); advantages and disadvantages; types of service provider (fixed-line operators, mobile network operators, internet service providers) and the services they offer, with Zimbabwean examples. [COM]

concepts.name: Postal and courier services
concepts.description: Agents of postal services (the national postal service and courier companies); services such as registered mail, recorded delivery, cash on delivery, poste restante, business reply service, freepost, franking machines and express mail; their importance and drawbacks. [COM]

concepts.name: Formal and informal communication and trends in business communication
concepts.description: Formal communication (business letters, memoranda, reports) and informal communication (the grapevine); advantages and disadvantages; drafting a business letter; trends such as email, video calls, social media and instant messaging, and the impact of ICT on business communication. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: The role of marketing and marketing concepts
concepts.description: Why marketing is needed: identifying and satisfying customer needs, customer loyalty and relationships, anticipating change; the production, product, selling and marketing concepts and their implications for a business. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Markets, demand and supply
concepts.description: Meaning of market, product, demand and supply; how demand and supply interact to set price, shown in simple diagrams described in words or tables. [BES]

concepts.name: Changing markets and market share
concepts.description: Why consumer spending patterns change, why markets become more competitive, how businesses respond; calculating market share. [CAM]

concepts.name: Types of markets: physical and virtual
concepts.description: Physical and virtual (online) markets, local, regional and global markets; their features, advantages and disadvantages. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Mass and niche markets
concepts.description: Mass marketing and niche marketing: concepts, advantages and disadvantages. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Market segmentation
concepts.description: Segmenting markets by age, income, location, gender, lifestyle and interests; reasons for segmentation; advantages and disadvantages. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Market research
concepts.description: Why businesses carry out market research; primary methods (questionnaires, surveys, interviews, focus groups, observation) and secondary sources; qualitative and quantitative data; sampling; designing data-collection tools; presenting and interpreting results in tables and charts; accuracy of research data. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Demand forecasting
concepts.description: Why businesses forecast demand and simple qualitative and quantitative methods of forecasting (opinion of sales staff and experts, consumer surveys, trends from past sales). [BES]

concepts.name: Product: branding, packaging and new products
concepts.description: The product element of the marketing mix: brand image, the roles of packaging, developing new products and its advantages and disadvantages. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The product life cycle and extension strategies
concepts.description: Stages of the product life cycle (introduction, growth, maturity, decline), interpreting a product life cycle diagram, extension strategies and their advantages and disadvantages; recommending an extension strategy. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Pricing methods
concepts.description: Cost-plus, competitive, penetration, skimming and dynamic pricing; advantages and disadvantages; recommending a pricing method. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Place: channels of distribution
concepts.description: Channels of distribution from producer to consumer (direct, through retailers, through wholesalers and retailers, through agents); factors in choosing a channel; recommending a channel. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Promotion: advertising and sales promotion
concepts.description: Reasons for promotion; advertising (informative and persuasive; media such as radio, television, newspapers, billboards, leaflets, social media, targeted messages) and sales promotion (vouchers, loyalty and reward schemes, competitions, special offers, free samples); choosing promotion methods and designing an advertisement. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Marketing strategy: the marketing mix together
concepts.description: The importance of each element of the marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) and how they fit together; evaluating the impact of the mix; recommending an appropriate marketing mix for a given situation. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Entering foreign markets
concepts.description: Advantages of selling in other countries (more sales, spreading risk) and the challenges (cultural differences, lack of knowledge, legal requirements, payment and currency), and ways of reducing them. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Money and inflation
concepts.description: Origins of money and the problems of barter; characteristics (qualities) and functions of money; causes and effects of inflation. [COM]

concepts.name: Personal income, saving and investment
concepts.description: Sources of personal income; saving and methods of saving; reasons for saving; personal investments (for example savings accounts, shares, property, livestock) and reasons for investing; the difference between saving and investment. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Personal budgets, borrowing and financial advice
concepts.description: Drawing up a personal budget; reasons for borrowing and when not to borrow; borrowing options (overdraft, bank loan, trade credit, informal lenders); sources of financial advice; consequences of financial mismanagement. [COM]

concepts.name: Taxation
concepts.description: Why governments tax; direct and indirect taxes (for example income tax, corporate tax, value added tax, customs and excise duties); the legal obligation to pay tax; the role of the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA). [COM]

concepts.name: The banking system and commercial banks
concepts.description: Classification of banks; services of commercial banks: current and savings accounts, loans and overdrafts, bank cards, cheques, electronic transfers (including RTGS), automated teller machines, standing orders and other services; filling in banking documents. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: Other financial institutions
concepts.description: Merchant banks, finance houses, discount houses, building societies, the post office savings bank, development and small-enterprise finance institutions and microfinance institutions: the services each provides. [COM, BES]

concepts.name: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Functions of a central bank and of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (issuing notes and coins, banker to the government and to commercial banks, lender of last resort, monetary policy, supervising banks, managing foreign reserves). [COM]

concepts.name: Trends in banking
concepts.description: Telebanking, internet banking, mobile banking and mobile money, agency banking and money transfer agents; their impact on customers, banks and economic activity. [COM]

concepts.name: International financial institutions
concepts.description: International financial institutions such as the World Bank (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development), the International Monetary Fund and regional development banks: roles and their activities in developing countries such as Zimbabwe. [COM]

concepts.name: Why businesses need finance
concepts.description: Start-up capital, expansion, replacing non-current assets, new technology and working capital; short-term and long-term finance needs; long-term and short-term capital. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Sources of finance and choosing a source
concepts.description: Internal sources (owners' savings, retained profit, sale of assets, working capital) and external sources (share capital, loans, overdrafts, trade credit, leasing, hire purchase, debentures, venture capital, government grants, crowdfunding, family, friends and community sources); advantages and disadvantages; factors in choosing a source; recommending a source. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Shares and debentures
concepts.description: Ordinary and preference shares, debentures, the differences between shares and debentures and between ordinary and preference shares, and types of capital (authorised, issued, called-up, paid-up). [COM]

concepts.name: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange
concepts.description: Functions and importance of a stock exchange and the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) to the economy; stockbrokers and jobbers (market makers); speculators (bulls, bears and stags). [COM]

concepts.name: Securing investors
concepts.description: How enterprises attract investors: a favourable policy environment, good corporate governance, a reputable brand, a sound business plan and track record. [BES]

concepts.name: Working capital
concepts.description: Meaning and calculation of working capital (current assets minus current liabilities); the working capital cycle; why managing working capital matters and ways of managing it. [COM, BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Cash flow forecasts and cash budgets
concepts.description: Main features of a cash flow forecast (cash budget): inflows, outflows, net cash flow, opening and closing balances; completing, amending and interpreting a forecast (ZIMSEC learners also prepare a simple cash budget). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Cash and solving cash-flow problems
concepts.description: Why cash matters to a business; the difference between cash and profit; causes of short-term cash-flow problems and ways to overcome them (overdraft, delaying payments to suppliers, asking customers to pay sooner, delaying purchases of non-current assets). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Budgeting and budgets
concepts.description: Budgeting and budgets; types of budget (cash, sales, production, purchases); preparing a simple budget for an enterprise; importance and limits of budgeting. [BES]

concepts.name: Profit and why it matters
concepts.description: What profit is (revenue minus costs) and why profit matters to private-sector businesses: reward for risk-taking, source of finance, measure of success, attracting investors. [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The income statement (statement of profit or loss)
concepts.description: Main features of an income statement (revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses, profit); simple calculations from it and decisions based on it (ZIMSEC learners also prepare a simple one). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: The statement of financial position
concepts.description: Non-current and current assets, non-current and current liabilities, capital employed; calculating total assets, total liabilities and working capital; decisions based on the statement (ZIMSEC learners also prepare a simple one). [BES, CAM]

concepts.name: Business calculations: turnover, profit, stock turn, mark-up and margin
concepts.description: Turnover, cost of goods sold, gross profit and net profit, average stock and the rate of stock turnover, mark-up and margin and converting between them; interpreting the results. [COM]

concepts.name: Profitability ratios
concepts.description: Gross profit margin, profit (net profit) margin and return on capital employed (ROCE): calculating and interpreting them and comparing results over time or between businesses. [COM, CAM]

concepts.name: Liquidity ratios
concepts.description: The concept of liquidity; current ratio and acid test ratio, calculating and interpreting them. [CAM]

concepts.name: Users of accounts and limits of ratio analysis
concepts.description: Internal and external users of accounts and ratio analysis and the decisions they make with them (whether to lend, invest or supply); limitations of accounts and ratio analysis. [CAM]

concepts.name: Nature and purpose of insurance and assurance
concepts.description: Insurance and assurance and the difference between them; business and life risks; insurable and non-insurable risks; pooling of risks; the use of statistics in setting premiums; communal systems of insurance such as zunde ramambo (isiphala senkosi) and burial societies. [COM]

concepts.name: Principles of insurance
concepts.description: Utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity and proximate cause (with subrogation and contribution as consequences of indemnity), applied to examples. [COM]

concepts.name: Insurance procedures, documents and people
concepts.description: Taking out a policy (proposal form, prospectus, premium, cover note, policy) and making a claim (claim form, assessment, settlement); the roles of brokers, underwriters, actuaries and loss assessors. [COM]

concepts.name: Types of insurance policy
concepts.description: Policies such as fire, burglary and theft, motor, goods in transit, marine, fidelity guarantee, public liability and employer's liability: what each covers and which risks a business should insure. [COM]

concepts.name: Assurance policies, social security and export credit insurance
concepts.description: Whole life, endowment, term and funeral assurance and medical aid; benefits of assurance; why the National Social Security Authority (NSSA) was formed and what it provides; the purpose of export credit guarantee insurance (the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation). [COM]

concepts.name: ICT in insurance and assurance
concepts.description: E-insurance and e-assurance (online quotations, policies, premium payments and claims); advantages and disadvantages of ICT in insurance for firms and clients. [COM]
